title: Leading People Who Are in Denial
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article addresses one of leadership's hardest coaching problems: someone in genuine denial about a flaw everyone else can see, often protected by an echo chamber of enablers who won't confront them. It notes that direct confrontation with facts typically backfires, deepening both the denial and defensiveness. As a less-conventional alternative, the piece describes leaders mirroring the negative behavior themselves — sometimes in exaggerated form — to make the point nonverbally, while acknowledging the real risk that the deflected mirroring reads as mockery rather than instruction. It closes by insisting the discomfort of confronting a denier is worth it, both for the people affected by the unaddressed behavior and, ultimately, for the person in denial themselves.
points: People in denial are often protected by an echo chamber of enablers who consciously avoid confronting the pattern others see clearly.
Direct confrontation with facts typically backfires, deepening both denial and defensiveness rather than resolving it.
Mirroring the negative behavior back at the person, sometimes in exaggerated form, is offered as a nonverbal alternative — with the real risk it reads as mockery.
The piece argues the discomfort of confronting a denier is worth bearing, both for those affected by the behavior and for the denier's own growth.
quotes: They refuse to accept any reality or facts that make them too uncomfortable. To preserve their self-image and to avoid shame or anxiety, they vehemently disallow any acknowledgment of a pattern known well to others.
Many leaders have learned the hard way that simply confronting those in denial with the facts usually makes matters worse.
What makes the situation even harder is the fact that many people in denial are empowered to do so by others.
By becoming a living example of the flawed behavior or pattern, a leader lets the action speak for them, often without any commentary.
In addition to the negative effect an unaddressed dysfunction has on others, living in denial stalls personal growth and escalates conflicts in relationships.
